title: Rebalance Profile account, security, and sign-in methods layout
description:
Problem: the continued visual-density review found `/profile` using the first visible area for account fields and the local password form, while linked sign-in methods and provider actions begin below the fold. This makes the security state and linked authentication methods less discoverable even though they are often the most important profile information.

Desired outcome: Profile should make identity, role, linked sign-in methods, and security actions scannable without burying important account state or overexposing identifiers.

Scope:
- In scope: Profile section hierarchy, compact account summary, password/security form placement, sign-in method row/card layout, linked-provider affordances, and coordination with TSK-0010 destructive confirmations and TSK-0138 privacy masking.
- Out of scope: adding new profile fields already tracked by TSK-0033 or changing authentication provider behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sign-in methods and account/security status are visible or directly reachable from the first viewport.
- Account summary, role, and security actions have a clearer hierarchy than editable text fields alone.
- Linked provider rows remain scannable after privacy masking and destructive-action confirmation work.
- Password/change actions do not crowd unrelated profile metadata.

Validation:
- Capture `/profile` before/after at narrow and desktop widths.
- Run focused browser checks for account save, password change validation, link-provider affordance visibility, and remove-action confirmation integration.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 continued visual-density review: `/profile` puts sign-in methods and linked-provider actions below the first visible area while account/password forms consume the top of the page.
